meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.18% to 25,299.35 as Nifty Bank gained 1.19%; October retail inflation came in at 6.09%; Brent settled at $95.82 and US shares slipped.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Fri 13 Nov: NIFTY 50 edges up to 25,299.35 as banks gain; October inflation at 6.09%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 0.18% to 25,299.35 and the Sensex 0.04% to 81,911.01 in a session that swung between small gains and losses, while Nifty Bank gained 1.19% to 61,518.50 as financial and realty shares rose (Angel One, Business Standard, Liquide, Kotak Neo).

India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit and the 5.93% forecast in a Reuters poll; SBI Research now expects a 25 basis point rise at the RBI's 2 to 4 December review (Reuters, Business Today).
Foreign investors bought a net ₹7,831 crore and domestic institutions sold ₹6,331 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo). The rupee closed 33 paise weaker at a provisional 94.04 per dollar (PTI).

Overseas, US shares fell about 0.4% after Nvidia's chief executive resigned, the US 10-year yield rose to about 5.10%, Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 and gold futures fell 2.88% (AP, CappNotes, Reuters).

outlook.headline: Inflation above 6%, crude near $96 and US yields above 5% frame Friday's session

drivers.title: Inflation and the RBI
drivers.text: October retail inflation rose to 6.09% from 5.54%, with consumer food inflation at 8.94% (Reuters, Business Today). SBI Research now expects a 25 basis point rise at the RBI's 2 to 4 December review rather than 50, and Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis expects 25 or 50 (Business Today). Rate expectations reach bond yields, deposit rates and loan rates.

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 on Thursday after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy sites, having fallen about $1 in early Asian trade (Reuters). India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: The rupee and bonds
drivers.text: The rupee closed 33 paise weaker at a provisional 94.04 per dollar as the dollar firmed (PTI), and the 10-year G-Sec yield was about 7.25%, up 4 basis points (Trading Economics). A weaker rupee raises the cost of imports; bond prices fall when yields rise.

drivers.title: Foreign flows and index changes
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹73,566 crore in the cash market from 1 to 12 Nov (provisional, Kotak Neo). Separately, Nuvama estimates about $2 billion of passive inflows from MSCI's November index review, effective 30 Nov (Business Standard). Foreign flows feed into large-cap prices and the rupee.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: The S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq each fell about 0.4% on Thursday and the Russell 2000 fell 1.7% (AP). Moves on Wall Street tend to shape foreign investors' appetite for emerging market shares, including India's.

global_cues.title: US yields, the Fed and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US 10-year yield rose back above 5% to about 5.10% and the dollar index to 103.19 (CappNotes). CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December near 85% (Investing.com). Higher US yields and a firmer dollar tend to weigh on the rupee and on foreign flows into Indian bonds and shares.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Thursday Japan's Nikkei fell 0.7% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng 1.26% (AP, CappNotes). On Friday morning Japanese and Korean shares opened higher as chip stocks rose (TradingKey).

us.title: The session
us.text: Wall Street ended slightly lower after a volatile day: the three main indices each fell about 0.4% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.7% (AP).

us.title: Nvidia
us.text: Nvidia said Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive, with finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO; the shares fell more than 13% at the open and closed 4.3% lower (Nvidia filing, ABC News).

us.title: Rates
us.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose back above 5% to about 5.10% as traders priced further Fed rises; Governor Christopher Waller said on Tuesday that a half-point rise could be warranted if data came in hot (CappNotes, Investing.com).

events.title: Oil rebounds on Gulf supply risks
events.text: Brent rose 3.3% after Houthi-claimed attacks on Saudi energy sites and President Trump's post that the US did not need a deal with Iran; higher OPEC+ output and US inventories limited the gain (Reuters). The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

commentary.text: Spot gold has fallen 5.2% over five sessions, after October's US consumer prices rose more than forecast and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point rise could be warranted if data came in hot (Investing.com).
The 10-year Treasury yield moved back above 5% and the dollar stayed firm, which weighs on gold because it pays no interest; oil's 3.3% rise added to inflation concerns (Kitco).
David Morrison of Trade Nation said gold and silver had not yet broken their cycle lows and that much may depend on the US dollar (Investing.com).

stories.headline: MSCI will add LIC, Coforge, Adani Green Energy and Meesho to its India index from 30 Nov
stories.what: MSCI's November review adds four companies to the MSCI India standard index and removes PI Industries, effective 30 November. Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research estimates India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index will rise to 11.7% from 11.5% (Business Standard, Kotak Neo).
stories.why: Index changes direct passive foreign money into added stocks and out of removed ones around the effective date, and India's overall weight affects how much benchmark-tracking money comes into Indian shares.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, an ELSS (equity linked savings scheme, often called a tax saver fund) must keep at least 80% of its assets in equity and equity-related instruments, and it follows the Equity Linked Saving Scheme, 2005, notified by the Ministry of Finance. With at least four-fifths of the portfolio in shares, its value can rise and fall with the stock market. Each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: What the retail inflation number measures
paragraphs: India's monthly retail inflation figure measures how much the prices of a basket of goods and services that households buy have changed from a year earlier.

In October it was 6.09%, up from 5.54% in September, and consumer food inflation was 8.94% (Reuters, Business Today). Food prices can move the figure noticeably: onion prices were up 116.22% from a year earlier (Business Today).

The RBI's tolerance band has an upper limit of 6%, so a reading above it feeds into expectations for the policy rate, which economists at SBI Research and Bank of Baroda have discussed ahead of the RBI's 2 to 4 December review (Business Today, Hello Banker).
